title: Arbitrary-positive-H conformastatic Ricci and Einstein components

items.title: Positive-scalar conformastatic chart data
items.design_state: Complete local definition or conditional proof authored with the exact planned claim and stated mathematical hypotheses.
items.statement:
Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open and let $H:D\to(0,\infty)$ be of class $C^3$, meaning that every partial derivative of total order at most three exists and is continuous. Set $\mathcal M:=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times D$, an open subset of $\mathbb R^4$, with global coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$; each coordinate is assigned length units, with $x^0=ct$ when a time coordinate is wanted. The function $H$ depends only on $(x^1,x^2,x^3)$ and is dimensionless.

Give $\mathcal M$ the coordinate orientation determined by $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$.

Define the symmetric coordinate tensor $g_H$ by
$$g_H=-H^{-2}(dx^0)^2+H^2\sum_{i=1}^3(dx^i)^2,$$
where $H^{-1}:=1/H$ and $H^{-2}:=(1/H)^2$. This exact coordinate form is called the positive-scalar conformastatic chart tensor in this item; no field equation or physical solution property is part of the definition.

For this $C^3$ chart tensor, a **time orientation** means a continuous selection at each $p\in\mathcal M$ of one of the two connected components of $\{v\in T_p\mathcal M:g_H(v,v)<0\}$, with the topology from the coordinate identification $T\mathcal M=\mathcal M\times\mathbb R^4$. Specify the selection globally by
$$C_p^+:=\left\{v=v^0\partial_0+\sum_{i=1}^3v^i\partial_i:g_H(v,v)<0,\ v^0>0\right\}.$$
Here the selection is continuous in the explicit sense that the fiberwise linear coordinate map $(p,v)\mapsto(p,v^0/H(p),H(p)v^1,H(p)v^2,H(p)v^3)$ is a continuous bundle isomorphism carrying $C^+$ to the constant cone $\{(u^0,\mathbf u):u^0>\|\mathbf u\|_2\}$; this map and its inverse are $C^3$. That cone and its negative are convex and nonempty, and a timelike vector has nonzero $u^0$, so they are exactly the two timelike components. Define a nonzero causal vector by $g_H(v,v)\le0$ and call it **future-directed** when $v^0>0$. Set $N_H:=H\partial_0$, a $C^3$ vector field (smooth if $H$ is smooth). The Lorentzian lemma below verifies $g_H(N_H,N_H)=-1$, so $N_H\in C_p^+$ everywhere. No smoothness beyond $C^3$ is required for this definition.


Because $H>0$, the functions $H^{-1}$ and $H^{-2}$ are compositions and products of $H$ with positive-base powers of exponents $-1$ and $-2$. The derivative formula for these powers, repeated through any finite order, and closure of $C^k$ functions under composition and finite products show that the displayed coefficients are $C^3$ when $H$ is $C^3$, and smooth when $H$ is smooth.

For later component formulas define $H_i:=\partial_iH$, $H_{ij}:=\partial_i\partial_jH$, $q:=\sum_{i=1}^3H_i^2$, and $\Delta H:=\sum_{i=1}^3H_{ii}$.

items.title: The positive-scalar conformastatic chart tensor is Lorentzian
items.design_state: Complete local definition or conditional proof authored with the exact planned claim and stated mathematical hypotheses.
items.statement: For every $D,H,g_H$ in [[def-emg-conformastatic-chart-data]], the coordinate tensor $g_H$ is a C3 nondegenerate Lorentzian metric of signature $(-,+,+,+)$. Its inverse components are $g^{00}=-H^2$ and $g^{ij}=H^{-2}\delta_{ij}$, its determinant is $-H^4$, and $\sqrt{|\det g|}=H^2$. The vector fields $n:=H\partial_0$ and $e_i:=H^{-1}\partial_i$ form a global orthonormal frame with $g(n,n)=-1$, $g(n,e_i)=0$, and $g(e_i,e_j)=\delta_{ij}$. The chosen time orientation makes $n$ future-directed, and the frame $(n,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is positively oriented.

items.title: Exact smooth superharmonic counterpoised dust family
items.design_state: Complete local definition or conditional proof authored with the exact planned claim and stated mathematical hypotheses.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as in [[def-countable-choice]], as required by the currently inspected general geometric convention in [[def-emg-matter-formal-systems]]. Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open and let $H\in C^\infty(D,(0,\infty))$ satisfy $\Delta H\le0$. Use $\mathcal M=\mathbb R\times D$, its coordinate orientation, and the time orientation for which $n:=H\partial_0$ is future, all as fixed in [[def-emg-conformastatic-chart-data]] and verified in [[lem-emg-conformastatic-chart-is-lorentzian]]. Use the metric $g_H$ and coordinates $x^0=ct,x^i$ of [[def-emg-conformastatic-chart-data]]. Fix formal constants $c,\mu_0,G_N>0$, put $\epsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$, $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$, and define the positive charge-to-mass parameter $Q_s:=\sqrt{4\pi\epsilon_0G_N}$ using the positive root of [[def-emg-explicit-power-regimes]]. For a sign $s\in\{-1,+1\}$ set
$$A:=s\frac{c}{Q_s}H^{-1}dx^0,\qquad F:=dA,\qquad U:=cH\partial_0,\qquad \rho:=-\frac{c^2\Delta H}{4\pi G_NH^3},\qquad \sigma:=sQ_s\rho,\qquad j:=\sigma U,\qquad T_m^{ab}:=\rho U^aU^b.$$
Let $a^b:=U^a\nabla_aU^b$ be the covariant four-acceleration of the timelike field $U$. Then $U=cn$ is future timelike with $g_H(U,U)=-c^2$, all displayed fields are smooth, and $\rho\ge0$. On $\{\rho>0\}$ the charge-to-mass ratio is $\sigma/\rho=sQ_s$; no ratio is defined by division at $\rho=0$. The tuple satisfies the formal sourced Maxwell equations $dF=0$, $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$, the dust matter exchange equation $\nabla_aT_m^{ab}=F^b{}_cj^c$, and the formal Einstein equation with $\Lambda=0$,
$$G_{ab}=\kappa\bigl(T_{m,ab}+T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}\bigr),$$
where $T^{\mathrm{EM}}$ is exactly the tensor of [[def-emg-matter-formal-systems]]. Its total stress satisfies WEC, NEC, SEC, and DEC. The coordinate four-acceleration of the static dust field is $a^0=0$, $a^i=-c^2H_i/H^3$, and its Lorentz force per unit mass balances it wherever $\rho>0$; the undivided exchange identity also holds where $\rho=0$.

This is a conditional mathematical solution family for the stated formal equations. It makes no claim of physical realization, equilibrium stability, or coupled-field existence for arbitrary initial data.

items.title: Globally regular sphere, proper integrals and dilute bounds
items.design_state: Complete local definition or conditional proof authored with the exact planned claim and stated mathematical hypotheses.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as stated in [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $a,b>0$ have length units, let $s\in\{-1,+1\}$, and on all of $\mathbb R^3$ set
$$r^2=(x^1)^2+(x^2)^2+(x^3)^2,\qquad \Psi(x):=\sqrt{r^2+b^2}>0,\qquad H(x):=1+\frac a{\Psi(x)}.$$
Use the constants and exact formal coupled family of [[thm-emg-smooth-counterpoised-dust]]. The function $H$ is smooth, positive, and satisfies
$$\Delta H=-\frac{3ab^2}{(r^2+b^2)^{5/2}}<0,\qquad \rho(x)=\frac{3c^2ab^2}{4\pi G_NH(x)^3(r^2+b^2)^{5/2}}.$$
On the slice $x^0=\text{constant}$ the induced spatial metric is $h=H^2\delta_{ij}dx^i dx^j$. Define the candidate proper mass and signed charge by
$$M_{\mathrm{prop}}:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\rho H^3\,d\lambda_3,\qquad Q_{\mathrm{prop}}:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\sigma H^3\,d\lambda_3.$$
The proof establishes that the first is a finite nonnegative Lebesgue integral and the second is a finite signed Lebesgue integral. They equal
$$M_{\mathrm{prop}}=\frac{c^2a}{G_N},\qquad Q_{\mathrm{prop}}=sQ_s\frac{c^2a}{G_N}.$$
The scalar curvature is $S_g=-2\Delta H/H^3>0$, the total stress satisfies WEC, NEC, SEC, and DEC, and the smooth matter density is positive at every point and has infinite spatial extent. For $a=\delta b$ with $0<\delta\le1$, put $h_0(x):=b/\sqrt{r^2+b^2}$ and
$$\rho_{\mathrm{lin}}(x):=\frac{3c^2\delta b^3}{4\pi G_N(r^2+b^2)^{5/2}}.$$
The same exact coupled solutions obey the pointwise Cartesian-coordinate bounds
$$\left|g_{00}+\bigl(1-2\delta h_0\bigr)\right|\le3\delta^2,\qquad \left|g_{ij}-\bigl(1+2\delta h_0\bigr)\delta_{ij}\right|\le\delta^2,\qquad 0\le1-\frac{\rho}{\rho_{\mathrm{lin}}}\le3\delta.$$
These are ideal mathematical estimates, not measurements or stability statements.

title: Arbitrary-positive-H conformastatic Ricci and Einstein components — Examples

items.title: Regular smooth counterpoised sphere
items.design_state: Complete local definition or conditional proof authored with the exact planned claim and stated mathematical hypotheses.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $b>0$ have length units, let $\mathbf{x}=(x^1,x^2,x^3)\in\mathbb R^3$, and define its Euclidean radius by $r:=\sqrt{(x^1)^2+(x^2)^2+(x^3)^2}$. Take $a=b$ and $s=+1$ in the exact family of [[thm-emg-smooth-counterpoised-dust]], and define $H(\mathbf{x})=1+b/\sqrt{r^2+b^2}$ on all of $\mathbb R^3$. For the family field strength $F$, set $n:=H\partial_0$, $e_i:=H^{-1}\partial_i$, and define the static-frame electric components by $E_i:=cF(e_i,n)$ for $i=1,2,3$. This is an everywhere regular smooth solution with center values
$$H(0)=2,\qquad \nabla H(0)=0,\qquad \Delta H(0)=-\frac3{b^2},\qquad \rho(0)=\frac{3c^2}{32\pi G_Nb^2},\qquad S_g(0)=\frac3{4b^2},\qquad E_i(0)=0.$$
Its proper mass and signed charge are $c^2b/G_N$ and $Q_sc^2b/G_N$, respectively. The model density is positive everywhere, so its topological support, defined as the closure in $\mathbb R^3$ of $\{\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb R^3:\rho(\mathbf{x})\ne0\}$, is all of $\mathbb R^3$.

items.title: Quantified dilute exact coupled family
items.design_state: Complete local definition or conditional proof authored with the exact planned claim and stated mathematical hypotheses.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $b>0$ have length units and let $\delta$ be dimensionless with $0<\delta\le1/10$. Put $a=\delta b$ and choose either charge sign $s\in\{-1,+1\}$ in the exact coupled family. For $\mathbf{x}=(x^1,x^2,x^3)\in\mathbb R^3$, define the Euclidean radius $r:=\sqrt{(x^1)^2+(x^2)^2+(x^3)^2}$ and $h_0(\mathbf{x}):=b/\sqrt{r^2+b^2}$, so $H=1+\delta h_0$. Then
$$\left|g_{00}+\bigl(1-2\delta h_0\bigr)\right|\le3\delta^2\le\frac3{100},\qquad \left|g_{ij}-\bigl(1+2\delta h_0\bigr)\delta_{ij}\right|\le\delta^2\le\frac1{100},\qquad 0\le1-\frac{\rho}{\rho_{\mathrm{lin}}}\le3\delta\le\frac3{10},$$
where $\rho_{\mathrm{lin}}=3c^2\delta b^3/[4\pi G_N(r^2+b^2)^{5/2}]$. These are exact ideal-family bounds, not measured errors. On $\mathcal M=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times\mathbb R^3$, the static dust velocity field is $U=cH\partial_0$. For each fixed $\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb R^3$ and $x^0_*\in\mathbb R$, define its static worldline by
$$\gamma_{\mathbf{x},x^0_*}:\mathbb R\to\mathcal M,\qquad \gamma_{\mathbf{x},x^0_*}(\tau):=(x^0_*+cH(\mathbf{x})\tau,\mathbf{x}).$$
This is a smooth future-directed timelike curve with $\dot\gamma=U$ and $g_H(\dot\gamma,\dot\gamma)=-c^2$; $\tau\in\mathbb R$, measured in seconds, is its proper-time parameter in the adopted length-coordinate convention. Here a static worldline is freely falling exactly when it is a geodesic, $\nabla_{\dot\gamma}\dot\gamma=0$, with $\nabla$ the connection of the exact family. Define the model's electromagnetic force per unit mass by $f^b:=(\sigma/\rho)F^b{}_cU^c$; this is defined everywhere for this profile since $\rho>0$. For this profile, $H_i=-\delta b x^i/(r^2+b^2)^{3/2}$, so when $r>0$ both $a^i$ and $f^i$ are nonzero and $a^i=f^i$. At $r=0$ both vectors vanish, and the central static worldline is geodesic.
